newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft eyes British, U.S. asset managers.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft eyes British, U.S. asset managers.

text.p: Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG said on Wednesday it remained interested in buying a foreign asset management firm and had made contact with several prospective candidates in Britain and the U.S.

"We have commissioned a British investment bank to look for candidates," Wolfgang Steinriede, one of two chief executives in Bankgesellschaft's management board, told Reuters after a news conference here.
"We have made contact with at least two asset management firms in London and one in the U.S. but we have not entered into any talks yet," Steinriede said.
He said the bank was interested in buying a majority stake in an asset manager.
Bankgesellschaft had eyed British fund manager Gartmore Plc but lost out to National Westminster Bank which said in February it was buying Gartmore for 472 million pounds.
Several large German banks have bought British and U.S. asset managers in recent years to strengthen their activities in what they see as a growing business.
Among the biggest deals were Commerzbank's acquisition of London-based Jupiter Tyndall and Dresdner's purchase of U.S. fund manager R.C.M. Capital management last year.
Bankgesellschaft said it was continuing to expand its investment banking activities and now had 300 staff in London.
